title: recommendations for consistent character and scene art?
author: sb1980
selftext:
hi all,

I am trying to build a simple adventure using ai for the art as I am no designer

I am struggling to build consistent artwork for scenes, items and characters

  
right now my workflow is to create a full scene and then to extract the objects and replace with the continuation of the background (e.g. a bottle someone picks up from a table to disappear).

characters I do separate by giving the scene , but no matter which tool I use, they always look very different in style, proportions don't match etc

  
which tools and flows are you using for this?

  
thanks

comments.author: Calm_Look_3206
comments.body: I’m building something right now, launching next week. Going to be a game changer for game devs.

comments.author: iiithewizardiii
comments.body: Is the intention to end up with still artwork across the board? (then I have a suggestion)

replies.author: sb1980
replies.body: Yes i am going for non animated at this point

replies.author: iiithewizardiii
replies.body: then having done this myself (over and over with multiple systems), I've landed on the best consistency + adherence to specific style to be combining a custom created SREF in Midjourney (using their Style Creator) coupled with a Moodboard that you continue to add to with the best results that you get. That will tighten and tighten the look. If you're doing BOTH characters and environs, its a little trickier but it can be done

comments.author: PhotojournalistBig53
comments.body: Both new openai and Gemini nano banana 2 do almost perfect img2img pose/style transfer if you wanna keep it consistent. You might have to do some minor edits in photoshop/gimp.

comments.author: Ok-Suspect-9855
comments.body: My favourite is Grok Imagine and use one image for reference and then all the games scenes have this same style reference and description or simple hand drawn sketch of the scene i want. I tell it to use the style refernece but make this description or build it like this sketch.

comments.author: cyberfire101
comments.body: for adventure game art you'll want to nail down a single model and seed setup in comfyui so proportions stay locked between scenes. Mage Space keeps characters looking the same across multiple shots without that manual workflow, which would fix your style-mismatch isue.

comments.author: False_Blackberry1269
comments.body:
man yeah, been there… it gets messy fast if you don’t lock things down early. what helped me was basically treating it like “training” the AI. Just pick a look, keep the same seed, reuse the same refs, don’t keep changing prompts every run or it drifts like crazy.

also kinda underrated, but having ziva is better, since it keeps characters behaving more consistently in Godot. not magic, but definitely less headache lol

comments.author: West_Rutabaga3310
comments.body: ive been using [gentube](https://www.gentube.app/p/world-builder?_cid=wb) to map out my worlds and characters and it's pretty consistent if you create a character block. also like that its free and unlimited

comments.author: Lazy-Western8139
comments.body: man yeah been there! consistency falls apart fast if you keep changing prompts every run. what helped me was reusing the same refs/seed and keeping everything organized in ziva so i stop losing the prompts that worked lol

comments.author: BugaiGames
comments.body:
Ai platforms has great results and features, but we found out that for production scale you need local generation eg ComfyUI.
There you have several tricks to help:
1. Very detailed prompt. If you want something to not change - include it in prompt
2. Same model, loras, seed and other parameters including resolution
3. When getting one character asset - try using it instead of latent input / IPadapter or inpaint changes. For scenes mostly IPAdapter, but it is a challendge in general.
4. Sometimes making video and cutting needed frame helps, as some of videos can be more character consistent than image regenaration

Hardcore option - train a Lora per character. Require investment into initial set and a lot of computing to retrain / experiment
